Appearance
From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Belle, bèlle, Bellé, belle-, and beḷḷẽ

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From French belle (“beautiful”), from Latin bella.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bɛl/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Audio (US):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛl
  • Homophone: bell

Noun

[edit]

belle (plural belles)

  1. An attractive woman.
    In her new dress she felt like the belle of the ball.
  2. (dated) A fellow gay man.[1]

Derived terms

[edit]
  • aquabelle
  • belle dame sans merci
  • belledom
  • Belle Époque
  • bellehood
  • cagebelle
  • croshabell
  • southern belle
  • volleybelle

Translations

[edit]
beautiful woman
  • Belarusian: прыгажу́ня f (pryhažúnja), красу́ня f (krasúnja)
  • Bulgarian: краса́вица (bg) f (krasávica)
  • Chinese:
    Mandarin: 美女 (zh) (měinǚ), 美人 (zh) (měirén)
  • Czech: kráska (cs) f, krasavice (cs) f
  • Esperanto: belulino
  • Finnish: kaunotar (fi)
  • French: belle (fr) f, beauté (fr) f
  • German: Schönheit (de) f, Schöne (de) f
  • Hindi: रमणी (hi) f (ramaṇī)
  • Japanese: 美人 (ja) (びじん, bijin), 美女 (ja) (びじょ, bijo), 別嬪 (ja) (べっぴん, beppin)
  • Macedonian: убавица f (ubavica)
  • Polish: piękność (pl) f
  • Portuguese: beldade (pt) f, bela (pt) f
  • Russian: краса́вица (ru) f (krasávica), красо́тка (ru) f (krasótka)
  • Serbo-Croatian:
    Cyrillic: лепотица f, љепотица f, лепојка f, љепојка f
    Latin: lepotica (sh) f, ljepotica (sh) f, lepojka f, ljepojka (sh) f
  • Slovak: krásavica f, kráska f
  • Slovene: lepotica f
  • Turkish:
    Ottoman Turkish: كوزل (güzel, gözel)
  • Ukrainian: красу́ня f (krasúnja)

Latin

Etymology

[edit]

From bellus (“pretty, handsome”).

[edit]

bellē (comparative bellius, superlative bellissimē)

  1. well, neatly, perfectly
  2. prettily, delightfully

Old English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • bell

Etymology

[edit]

    From Proto-West Germanic *bellā, from Proto-Germanic *bellǭ.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈbel.le/, [ˈbeɫ.ɫe]

    Noun

    [edit]

    belle f

    1. bell
      bellan hringan
      to ring a bell
      • late 10th century, Ælfric, "St. Benedict, Abbot"
        Se dēofol wearp ānne stān tō þǣre bellan þæt hēo eall tōsprang.
        The Devil threw a rock at the bell so it broke into pieces.

    Declension

    [edit]

    Weak n-stem:

    singular plural
    nominative belle bellan
    accusative bellan bellan
    genitive bellan bellena
    dative bellan bellum

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • Middle English: belle
      • Scots: bell
      • English: bell
        • → Fiji Hindi: belo
        • → Japanese: ベル (beru)
        • → Korean: 벨 (bel)

    Turkish

    [edit]

    Verb

    [edit]

    belle

    1. second-person singular imperative of bellemek
